title: Every household in this rural town will get $10,000 if a data center gets built
source_used: Yahoo (syndicated copy citing the Wall Street Journal)
key_facts: NorthPoint Development has been sending letters since June saying each Hazle Township, Pennsylvania household would get $10,000 if its data center is approved.
The township has roughly 4,500 households; median household income is about $60,000.
The data center is part of a plan for 15 buildings on 1,300 acres in the Pocono foothills.
Residents worry about noise, property values and rural character; one retiree called the offer a possible bribe.
Township officials rejected the plan on zoning grounds last November; NorthPoint sued; the township has paused new data center construction while it revises zoning.
NorthPoint says it will also provide another $120 million over 15 years, including funding for a police department.
quote_evidence: A Pennsylvania township is considering an unusual trade-off: If a sprawling data center project wins approval, every household would get $10,000.
Last November, township officials rejected the data-center plan on zoning grounds, and NorthPoint later sued to try to reverse that decision.
why_it_matters_hint: Developers are now offering direct cash to households to win local approval.
event_date: letters from June 2026; WSJ report date not stated
notes: Yahoo copy of a syndicated article that relays the Wall Street Journal; the WSJ original was not opened.
